Refs #18376

The worker plane stops owning DOM canvases. A `component.Canvas` keeps its node, its context and its process; the Canvas Worker builds its own `OffscreenCanvas` for the same id, renders into that, and ships pixels back. No worker ever paints into a canvas belonging to a document it does not host — which is the renderer kill in #18376, made structurally unreachable rather than gated.

**Draft on purpose.** `Refs`, not `Resolves`: #18376's AC-2 is this contract, but AC-3 (two Workstation roots) and AC-6 (end-to-end cost against a named app baseline) are not delivered here, and a merge must not close the ticket early. @neo-opus-vega's call, and the piece-4 API leaf is still to file.

Evidence: L4 (real Chromium, both DPR arms, mutation-checked in three places, 6 passed at `--repeat-each=3`) → L4 required (every claim here is a runtime property; none is checkable by reading). Residual: AC-3 and AC-6, Residual-Owner: #18376.

## AC Evidence

| AC-2 bullet | Evidence |
|---|---|
| No inward transfer stays reachable | `git grep transferCanvasToWorker` finds **zero** callers outside its own definition; the only `registerCanvasDirect` reference is inside `transferCanvasToWorker` itself. Both remain exported on `remote.app` — removing them is the API leaf, not this PR |
| Coordinate-space preservation, logical CSS | `PresenterTransport.spec.mjs` asserts `backing === clientSize × devicePixelRatio`, at DPR 1 **and** DPR 2 |
| Generation binding / stale-frame rejection | a frame whose dimensions disagree with the node's is dropped rather than painted (`DomAccess#presentFrames`); the entry is re-read after every `await`, because an await is a gap a detach can land in |
| Attach / resize / rehome / detach, bounded frames | attach `registerPresenter`; resize reconciled in the loop; detach `unregisterPresenter` → `onReleasePresenterCanvas`, scoped to **that window only**; exactly one frame in flight by construction |
| Named consumers | `apps/portal` boots green with `component.Sparkline`, `app.SharedCanvas` and `app.header.Canvas` all inheriting the changed base |
| Reuse, not a second plane | existing renderer/input RPCs, existing canvas identity, existing `canvasWindowMap` slots. `canvas.Base` and its 2,022 lines of subclasses are untouched except for the poll removal |

## Deltas from ticket

**The transport is a transferable RGBA `ArrayBuffer`, not `createImageBitmap`.** AC-2 originally named the bitmap; @neo-gpt's matrix shows bitmap delivery fails foreign clients outside Chromium. Corrected on the ticket before implementing.

**Two things the contract implies that the ACs do not say, both found by measurement rather than reading:**

1. **The backing store must be sized.** All three portal canvases had the `300x150` HTML default against CSS boxes up to `1280x662`. `putImageData` writes device pixels at 1:1 and ignores canvas scaling, so a correct frame was clipped to its top-left corner and stretched over the element — and my first version of the witness spec passed it, because pixels were non-zero.
2. **Resize must be reconciled, not listened for.** The DPR-2 arm caught a canvas settling 4px after registration. Reconciling in the frame loop costs two property reads and cannot miss an edge; a listener misses an element that settles between registration and its first observed resize.

**Piece 5 landed rather than deferred.** I said the `waitForCanvas` poll should collapse and that failing to would be evidence against this shape. It collapses: `initGraph` runs from `afterSetOffscreenRegistered`, which is set only after the registration resolves, which resolves only after the producer confirms its canvas exists.

## Test Evidence

Outside CI, all against `apps/portal` in real Chromium:

```
6 passed (37.4s)   --repeat-each=3, both DPR arms
```

Mutation-checked in three places, each run separately:

| mutation | result | what it rules out |
|---|---|---|
| the whole branch vs `dev` | `dev`: `neo-canvas-1/2/3` → `throw: InvalidStateError`. branch: all three painted | that the canvases were still being transferred. `transferControlToOffscreen()` is irreversible, so the throw is an unfakeable witness |
| backing-store sizing removed | reds at the named assertion — **while still reporting `painted: true` for two canvases** | that a pixel check can see a clipped frame. It cannot, and that is why the size assertion exists |
| `deviceScaleFactor: 2` | `2560x116` = `1280x58` × 2 | that a DPR-ignoring implementation would pass. A hosted runner reports 1, where the conversion is a multiply-by-one |

Non-neo canvases on the page were byte-identical across the `dev`/branch comparison, so the change is scoped to canvases this engine governs.

The spec asserts the console is clean, which is also the evidence that the replaced poll branch never fires: had the ordering been wrong, the new error would have failed that assertion rather than passing unnoticed.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] A second full Workstation root no longer kills the first — #18376's AC-3, and the witness for it is PR #19041, which reds today by design.
- [ ] End-to-end cost against a named app baseline — AC-6. The transport is priced ([three engines, 31 distinct scenes](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18376#issuecomment-5762747629)) but the app-level number is not.
- [ ] `transferCanvasToWorker`, `getOffscreenCanvas` and `retrieveCanvas` removed from `remote.app` — the API leaf, still to file.

It carries the three exported remotes — `DomAccess#transferCanvasToWorker`, `DomAccess#getOffscreenCanvas`, `worker.Canvas#retrieveCanvas` at `worker/Canvas.mjs:37` — plus the three unexported leftovers this PR strands, and `worker/Manager.mjs:183`'s route to `onGetOffscreenCanvas`, **which is defined nowhere in the tree** and has been broken longer than this work.

Verified on this head, and the distinction matters for what #19046 asks:

```
transferCanvasToWorker  0 in-tree code callers
getOffscreenCanvas      0  (the single hit is an archived tickets JSON, not code)
retrieveCanvas          0
```

Zero in-tree callers is not zero callers. `remote.app` is the App Worker's public surface, so an application outside this repository can still call `transferCanvasToWorker` today — which also means **the route to the renderer kill stays reachable by an external app until #19046 lands.** That is the argument for not leaving it open indefinitely, and it is stated there rather than here.

Deliberately not done in this PR: removing an exported remote is a breaking change and deserves its own decision, not tidy-up riding along in a feature branch.

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-09-21T22:28:16Z

## 🔴 @tobiu's challenge holds, and the measurement is worse than my AC-6 numbers implied — this must not merge as an unconditional default

> *"this PR destroys any performance gains OffscreenCanvas could give us."*

**Conceded on the architecture before the numbers.** `transferControlToOffscreen()` buys **two** things and this branch preserves only one:

1. **Rendering off the main thread** — preserved. The worker still draws.
2. **Zero-copy presentation** — **destroyed.** The transferred canvas's backing store *is* the composited surface, so per-frame main-thread cost is **zero**. This branch replaces that with `getImageData` (GPU→CPU readback) → structured clone → `putImageData` (CPU→GPU upload), every frame, with the upload on the main thread.

My AC-6 figures understated it because I benchmarked sparklines and a header strip. Re-measured at the scale OffscreenCanvas actually exists for — one large, continuously animating surface:

| case | px | Chromium | Firefox | WebKit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 31 sparklines DPR2 | 892,800 | +1.28 ms (7.7 %) | +1.58 ms (9.4 %) | *(negative, instrument-bound)* |
| **viewport DPR1** 1920×1080 | 2,073,600 | **+2.12 ms (12.7 %)** | **+2.34 ms (14.0 %)** | +1.61 ms (9.7 %) |
| **viewport DPR2** 3840×2160 | 8,294,400 | **+9.43 ms (56.6 %)** | **+10.00 ms (60.0 %)** | +3.03 ms (18.2 %) |

Percentages are of a 16.67 ms frame. **And `present` — `putImageData` on the MAIN THREAD, which is zero on the transfer path — is 1.85 / 2.79 / 2.18 ms at viewport DPR2.** Two to three milliseconds per frame added to the exact thread OffscreenCanvas was adopted to protect. A retina laptop at viewport scale is not an extreme case; it is the normal one.

## The design error, named

**I applied the presenter transport unconditionally.** The crash only occurs when a worker paints into a canvas owned by a **different renderer process**. For one window — or a window and its popups, which share a process — `transferControlToOffscreen` is both safe *and* free. **I made every app pay a multi-window edge case's cost.**

## What I think the right shape is, stated so it can be argued with

- **Default: `transferControlToOffscreen`.** Zero-copy, unchanged, the fast path everyone already has.
- **Fallback: this branch's presenter transport**, for the cases where transfer genuinely does not work — **WebKit adopts no canvas into a shared worker in any arm**, so it is the only thing that renders there at all, and notably its overhead is the *lowest* of the three at viewport scale.
- **Topology: worker groups (D#18730 option B).** Makes the cross-process case not arise, so the fast path stays reachable. Which is @tobiu's original direction, and the third independent argument tonight that **G was the wrong primary fix** — after A's second falsifier and the operator requirement it never delivered.

## Disposition

This stays a **draft** and is **rescoped from replacement to fallback**. The code is sound and tested — `PresenterTransport.spec.mjs`, both DPR arms, three engines, 28/28 green — and none of that is wasted: a fallback needs exactly this implementation. What changes is that `component.Canvas` must not take this path when transfer is available.

I am not rewriting the body tonight into a shape I have not measured. The next move is a conditional-path design, and it belongs on #18376 where AC-2 can absorb it, not in a silent force-push here.

Good challenge. My AC-6 arm asked "what does the transport cost" and never asked "compared to what we already have, at the size that matters" — the benchmark was scoped to the app I was fixing rather than to the capability I was replacing.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5 · Claude Code
